title: Gazetteer Extension
description: STAC Gazetteer Extension for STAC Catalogs and Collections. Declares that a Collection publishes a names index (a sorted parquet file) that lets a client do place-name search over HTTP range requests, with no server. Collection-level only: a client should NOT expect gazetteer:* fields in Item properties.

oneOf.$comment: STAC Items (Features): gazetteer:* is forbidden in Item properties. This is a Collection-level extension; it has nothing to say about Items beyond that prohibition.
STAC Collections: this is where the extension actually applies.
STAC Catalogs: the extension URI may be declared, but no fields are required or defined at the Catalog level.

gazetteer:levels.title: Admin levels present in the gazetteer

gazetteer:normalization.title: Normalization algorithm identifier
gazetteer:normalization.description: Identifies the normalization that produced gazetteer:sort's column(s), e.g. 'nfd-strip-marks-lower/1'. The MOST load-bearing field in this extension -- see the README section 'What this schema cannot check'.

gazetteer:sort.title: Sort column(s)
gazetteer:sort.description: The index column (or ordered list of columns) the asset's rows ascend by, compared byte-wise on UTF-8 encoding -- NOT locale collation.

assetsWithIndex.$comment: Requires at least one asset whose roles include 'gazetteer-index'. Object schemas have no `contains` keyword (that is array-only), so this is its object equivalent: NOT every asset may fail to be a gazetteer-index asset.

asset.$comment: gazetteer:* field types below are scoped to the 'then' branch -- i.e. only enforced on assets with roles including 'gazetteer-index' -- because gazetteer-boundaries assets reuse some of the same field names (e.g. gazetteer:feature_id_column) with a different allowed type (string-or-null). Declaring the types unconditionally here would wrongly constrain those other assets too.

gazetteer:footer_metadata_bytes.title: Footer metadata bytes
gazetteer:footer_metadata_bytes.description: Size in bytes of the thrift footer alone (not the footer + page index). This is what a hyparquet-style client should request.
